- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% from prior 30d avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14d moving average, adjust forecast toward mean reversion (toward 14d MA) by 3–7%.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment median as weight to blend forecast with prior 14d trend.
